statement: A class of 20 scored a mean of 70. Another class of 30 scored a mean of 80. What is the mean of all 50 students?

choices.misconception: I weighted the means towards the smaller class by mistake.
I averaged the two means, which would only be right for equal class sizes.
I weighted correctly but divided by 49 rather than 50.
I added the two means rather than combining the totals.

hints: Add the two totals before dividing anything.
Turn each mean into a total by multiplying by the class size, add the two totals, then divide by the combined number of students. Means cannot be averaged when the groups differ in size.
The totals are 20 x 70 = 1400 and 30 x 80 = 2400, over 50 students.

solutions.reliable: The totals are 1400 and 2400, so 3800 points are spread over 50 students, giving a mean of 76. The transferable idea: a combined mean is a weighted one, so convert to totals and divide once at the end, which automatically weights each group by its size.
solutions.elegant: The larger class is 30 of the 50, so the answer sits three fifths of the way from 70 up to 80.

whyOnTest: Averaging the two means is the standard error, and the class sizes are deliberately unequal so that it gives a different answer.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
